# Nehemiah Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 471v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Now when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that no breach remained in it — though up to that time I had not yet set up the doors in the gates —

**2** Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono." But they intended to do me harm.

**3** I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"

**4** They sent to me four times in this way, and I answered them the same way each time.

**5** Then Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time with an open letter in his hand.

**6** In it was written: "It is reported among the nations — and Geshem confirms it — that you and the Jews are planning to rebel, and that is why you are building the wall. According to these reports, you are about to become their king.

**7** You have also set up prophets to proclaim concerning you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now these reports will reach the king. So come, let us take counsel together."

**8** I sent to him, saying, "Nothing like what you are saying has taken place. You are inventing it out of your own mind."

**9** For they were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will grow weak and drop from the work, and it will not be done." But now, O God, strengthen my hands.

**10** Then I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah son of Mehetabel, who was confined at home. He said, "Let us meet together in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you — they are coming to kill you by night."

**11** But I said, "Should a man like me flee? And could one like me enter the temple and live? I will not go in."

**12** I understood and saw that God had not sent him, but he had pronounced the prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

**13** For this purpose he was hired: that I should be afraid and act in this way and sin, so that they could give me a bad name in order to taunt me.

**14** Remember Tobiah and Sanballat, O my God, according to these things that they did, and also the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets who wanted to make me afraid.

**15** So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.

**16** When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid and fell greatly in their own esteem, for they perceived that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God.

**17** Moreover, in those days the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters were coming to them.

**18** For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

**19** They also kept reporting his good deeds in my presence and carrying my words back to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes
1. **6:5 "open letter"** — An unsealed letter was a deliberate act of public shaming; diplomatic correspondence was normally sealed. Sanballat intended the accusation to circulate widely.
2. **6:11 "could one like me enter the temple and live?"** — Nehemiah recognizes the theological trap: as a non-priest, entering the temple sanctuary would be a capital offense (Num 18:7), which would discredit him and his mission.
3. **6:15 "fifty-two days"** — The wall's completion in under two months was extraordinary, prompting even Israel's enemies to acknowledge divine assistance (v. 16).

*— LOGOS*
